Page 120

Before the forgotten dusk of the twenty - four deaths of OM (Past / Subtraction), his ancestral sons…

After the revealed dawn of the twenty - fourth birth of WO (Future / Addition), his childlike daughters…

  • All her children make her tremble, Ô ( World / Location ) the ultimate Rildée, enthused by the HISM ( Forces / Actions - at - Distance / Magic ), the dance of the assembly of tetraarchs in couples so close they make but one bicephalous whole ( beings sometimes wrongly named "the" SZIIZS ) though hating as much as adoring each other, each desiring and animating Ô through their symphony and discordance:
  • … IÔ ( H - H ) ÔI ( Dis - Assembly ) the lightning poet - perfuming,
  • … SÔ ( I - I ) ÔS ( De - Placement ) the undulating lover - honeying,
  • … MÔ ( S - S ) ÔM ( In - Tangibility ) the scree prophetess - blooming,
  • … HÔ ( M - M ) ÔH ( Dis - Order ) the blazing mystic - frosting.

All children of Ô, the Wo - of - Ô and Om - of - Ô, pull and push her by her cord, flaying their unique parent in all her limbs twisted with laughs and pains, through their passionate loves and fanatic hatreds.

  • Thus children of Ô, some directed and others led astray by the charm of her four orderers, torture then heal Ô and inversely - and from the tragic emotion of her suffered beauty bewitching and inspiring the tetraarchs choreographing their destructive dance of iôH-sôI-môS-hôM opposed to the founding one of Hôi-Iôs-Sôm-Môh, in the ballet of the HISM.
  • Thus children of Ô, in their discordance, some antagonizing and others uniting, play a delirious harmony from which is born and flows from their sweating efforts the unique WÔM ( Time / Count ), their siamese little brother - sister, perched far away and recon- ciling all through judgment establishing each one's wealth and designating how far each one's realms extend

All waltz without ever stopping with one another in the torpors of pain, yet dancing together with joy through their comforting reunion.

All have lived since always and forever, eternal through Ô being herself.
